speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; to begin my evaluation, how long have you noticed this area of concern?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background. Given your history of sunbathing and diabetes, what specific symptoms are you noticing on the back of your left hand, such as changes in color, texture, or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on a sun-exposed area (dorsal hand) in an elderly patient with a history of sunbathing is classic for this pre-malignant skin lesion.
